A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPBT research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and expanded material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on eight classification and reinforcement-learning tasks, component ablations, and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments replaying discovered hyperparameter schedules with fresh model initializations.

M1.justification: The restart criteria, step-size doubling, shrink-perturb, random reinitialization, and time-varying meta-BO remain unchanged. Appendix A expands previously described procedures into Algorithms 2–3; it does not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight tasks. The added replay experiments reuse CIFAR-10/100, Fashion-MNIST, and Humanoid with different training procedures and initializations, rather than adding datasets or task requirements. Transformer evaluation is proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same five PBT variants and RS, ASHA, and SMAC3. The new Humanoid replay analysis reuses ASHA, already evaluated against IPBT on that task; it introduces no distinct comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces a replay protocol: extract discovered schedules and train fresh weights using those schedules, retaining shrink-perturb at IPBT restarts. Humanoid replay also evaluates ASHA schedules. The original benchmark budgets, architectures, search spaces, and model-selection procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a substantive investigation of whether discovered schedules remain effective with fresh initializations, covering three classification tasks and Humanoid and revealing different behavior across these settings. Appendix E also assesses restart overhead. Existing ablations are retained, including the distillation comparison moved from Appendix F/Figure 10 to Appendix G/Figure 11.

E5.justification: New Tables 5–6 report IQM with interquartile ranges for original and replayed performance, adding a dispersion-reporting practice. The original eight-run evaluation, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, 50,000 significance-test replicates, and Holm correction remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 10 adds numerical breakdowns for six tasks previously represented only in aggregate comparisons. Tables 5–6 add replay results: CIFAR-100 IQM accuracy is 73.0 originally versus 73.4 on replay, while Humanoid scores are 9272 versus 6939 for IPBT and 8241 versus 6197 for ASHA. These are newly evaluated conditions; retained main results and Table 4 p-values are unchanged.

T1.justification: No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced. The added pseudocode expressions restate the existing stagnation criteria and shrink-perturb procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: task-agnostic restarts automatically adjust PBT step size and provide strong low-budget performance without per-task tuning. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds an applicability qualification: schedule replay preserves classification performance but loses performance in Humanoid, motivating treatment of PBT as weight training in unstable settings. The conclusion additionally identifies per-task tuning and evaluation with other architectures as unresolved directions.

D1.justification: Appendix A makes restart detection and reinitialization more explicit. Appendix E newly reports approximately 80 CPU-seconds for meta-BO and 0.5 seconds for weight adaptation, contextualized against approximately 1300 seconds for 1% of TinyImageNet training. Hardware disclosures and the code repository target are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds limited references concerning evolutionary restarts, checkpoint-based HPO, Transformers, and PBT as weight training: Auger and Hansen, Mehta et al., Vaswani et al., and Liu et al. (2022a). The main positioning relative to BG-PBT and other HPO methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include local terminology and explanation edits, numbered weight/HP subsections, expanded appendix organization, and added acknowledgments and an impact statement.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview schematic to Figure 1, two pseudocode displays, a six-panel task-results figure, and two replay tables. It also adopts conference formatting with running headers, revised typography, and restyled/repositioned tables and figures. Existing empirical plots are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through task-level scores, fuller pseudocode, and measured restart costs. The replay experiments add useful evidence about practical schedule reuse and expose its limitations in reinforcement learning. These are meaningful, targeted gains in reproducibility and applicability guidance, while the core method and primary comparative evidence remain stable.
